+*International transfers*+ 

In circumstances where an adequacy decision adopted by the European Commission does not apply, the legal basis that we rely on for the transfers of personal data to the recipients that are located outside of the EU/EEA is the Standard Contractual Clauses adopted by the EU Commission (on June 4, 2021). 

+*Retention*+

Bolt retains your data for only as long as necessary for the purposes described above. This means that we retain different categories of data for different periods of time depending on the type of data, the transportation service it relates to, and the purposes for which we collected the data.

* Your personal data will be stored as long as you have an active account. If your account is closed, personal data will be deleted (according to our retention schedule and rules), unless such data is still required to meet any legal obligation, or for accounting, dispute resolution or fraud prevention purposes.
* Financial data regarding transportation services provided to passengers will be stored for three years after the last journey. Data required for other accounting purposes will be stored for seven years after the last journey.
* In the event of a suspected criminal offence, fraudulent activity or false information having been provided, the data will be stored for up to 10 years.
* In case of payment disputes, data will be retained until the claim is satisfied or the expiry date of such claims.
* Journey history data and the data about usage of transportation services will be stored for three years, after which the data will be anonymised.
* Data on sensors for rental vehicles is stored for 6 months.

Please note that the deinstallation of Bolt app in your device does not cause the deletion of your personal data. If the Bolt app has not been used for three years, we’ll get in touch and ask you to confirm whether you wish to keep your account active for future use. If no reply is received in a reasonable time, the account will be closed and personal data will be deleted unless such data is required for any purpose mentioned earlier in this privacy notice.

 

+*Source of Personal Data*+

Your personal data originates from either your direct provision to Bolt or its collection through the Bolt platform.

+*Automated decision-making if you are a user of the rental services*+

*What personal data do we process?*

When you use our Bolt rental electric scooters, we process your personal data collected via the sensors of the scooter to ensure you are using our services in a safe manner. The type of data we process from scooters includes geolocation data, vehicle speed, motor power (including voltage and throttle level) and driving style information (including sudden braking or skidding). This data is used to identify reckless driving events, i.e. skidding, abrupt braking, tandem riding, bad parking and collisions.

*How do we process your personal data?*

Our internal monitoring system tracks each event that occurs whilst a user is using the scooter, assigns it a certain weight, then calculates an overall score for reckless driving and issues a warning once the user reaches a certain score threshold. The total score of the user is the sum of the reckless events over the last five rides.

If we detect any potentially dangerous behaviour then we will issue the user with a warning in the app to encourage them to refrain from using the scooter in a certain way. There are three levels of warnings:

#  *first warning* - informs the user about the risks of misbehaviour;
#  *second warning* - limits the speed of the scooter until the overall user score improves; and
#  *third warning* - temporarily suspends the user from the service. The user is able to contest the suspension by contacting our Customer Support Team for further information as to why their account was suspended.

For safety considerations, we cannot disclose the exact thresholds that trigger our warnings to prevent users from abusing the system.

We may also use automated decision-making in order to undertake fraud checks which are necessary for us to perform our services, ensure that the services are paid for and ensure the protection of riders from fraudulent transactions on their payment cards.

We may use automated decision-making in order to verify you which is necessary to ensure the safety of our platform and the enforcement of our terms and conditions.

We may also use automated decision-making for complaint resolution purposes. We may use the complaints information you provide to our customer support team via our chat function. The information relating to your complaints may be used to generate an automated response which will then be evaluated by a human agent to make the final decision.

In cases where we use automated processing or profiling that has a significant effect on your rights, you may have the right for human intervention and the right on grounds relating to your particular situation to object to the processing of personal data concerning you based on automated decisions/profiling as set out in section “Your rights and controls”, and to express your point of view and contest the outcome of the decision by contacting our customer support in our app.You may also be entitled to an explanation regarding the logic of making an automated decision.

For information on how we process relevant personal data, and for *Your Rights and Controls*, as well as *how to lodge a complaint with the competent supervisory authority*, we refer you to our Privacy Policy at [https://bolt.eu/de-de/privacy/privacy-for-riders/?category=rides|https://bolt.eu/de-de/privacy/privacy-for-riders/?category=rides|smart-link] 

*Your rights*

In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data, restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws.

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.

 

Yours sincerely, 

Bolt

*SQL query used*

{noformat}SELECT
    gateway,
    payment_method_type,
    acquirer_name,
    is_eea_country,
--    country,
    scheme_id_exists,
    COUNT(*)
FROM
    (
    SELECT
        p.payment_method_type,
        p.gateway,
        pmc.acquirer_name,
        sc.country_code AS country,
        (
            CASE 
                WHEN (p.card_scheme_id IS NOT NULL) THEN 'yes'
                ELSE 'no'
            END
        ) AS scheme_id_exists,
        (
            CASE 
                WHEN (sc.country_code IN (
                    'at', 'be', 'bg', 'hr', 'cy', 'cz', 'dk', 'ee', 'fi', 'fr', 'de', 'gr', 'hu', 'ie', 'it', 'lv', 'lt', 'lu', 'mt', 'nl', 'pl', 'pt', 'ro', 'sk', 'si', 'es', 'se', 'gb', 'gf', 'gp', 'mq', 'me', 'yt', 're', 'mf', 'gi', 'ax', 'pm', 'gl', 'bl', 'sx', 'aw', 'cw', 'wf', 'pf', 'nc', 'tf', 'ai', 'bm', 'io', 'vg', 'ky', 'fk', 'ms', 'pn', 'sh', 'gs', 'tc', 'ad', 'li', 'mc', 'sm', 'va', 'je', 'gg', 'gi'
                )) THEN 'yes'
                ELSE 'no'
            END
        ) AS is_eea_country
    FROM
        ng_public.payment_payment p
    JOIN ng_public.payment_payment_order po
        ON
        p.payment_order_id = po.id
    JOIN ng_public.admin_system_city sc
        ON po.city_id = sc.id
    JOIN ng_public.payment_payment_method_creation pmc
        ON
        pmc.payment_user_id = po.payment_user_id 
        AND
        pmc.payment_method_type = p.payment_method_type 
        AND
        pmc.payment_method_id = p.payment_method_id 
    WHERE
        p.created >= date '2024-02-28'
        AND p.state = 'captured'
        AND p.gateway = 'adyen'
        AND p.payment_method_type IN (
            'applepay',
            'googlepay',
            'processout'
        )
)
WHERE 
    scheme_id_exists = 'no'
GROUP BY
    gateway,
    payment_method_type,
    acquirer_name,
    is_eea_country,

ORDER BY

    payment_method_type,

Hey Tomasz,

The amount in the report is 402.0946 PLN, and the difference with the invoice is 0.0146 PLN. This is simply a rounding issue (which is not specific to Bolt, but happens quite often due to different decimal amounts used in calculations). This difference is coming from the decimal difference in the calculation of service fee:

As you can see in the report:

* Sum of service fee (net) in the report is 25.2882, while invoice only displays 25.28
* Sum of service fee VAT amount in the report is 5.8164, while the invoice only displays 5.81.

So, you can see that this is simply a rounding issue caused by the report using more decimals than the invoice. This is quite normal, and our balance system is smart enough to consider this rounded amounts once they reach 0.1+

Hello Marc! 
This particular driver was actioned through our fleet drivers' behaviour review. Please do note that we do comprehensive and detailed checks on the drivers and the type of fraud they engage in. Some drivers only misuse particular features and/or payment methods and overall perform well as supply at the same time. In those cases, their good behaviour often overwrites the bad they do.

Hence, the decision to limit in-app comes from this same logic that as a cash driver, this particular driver has proved to behave well and be beneficial to the supply. To block them fully would take this supply off while they only engaged in one particular type of fraud/scheme. Of course, should the local operations wish, we can consider a full block but then that would result in the supply and fleet as well being heavily affected. If the driver over time proves to have a great work ethic and ‘learns’ from the improper behaviour, we can also decide to add back the in-app option. 

In conclusion, the limitation of certain options can help Bolt save from fraud but also keep the supply going. There are just a couple of drivers affected by these checks.

In case you need to explain further you can advise that the driver will have certain options limited due to their previous non-adherence to our T&C. 

Cheers,

Hey, I’m adding a little bit more context of how this “speed threshold” would be calculated.

We measured average from 7% of all couriers (took 145 couriers that were the slowest ones). Avg speed of those slowest couriers was our threshold. So blockings would only affect 41 courier (that delivers less than 2% of our active supply). 

By blocking only the very worst couriers would decrease pickup delays by 5.88 % (or 1 pp). 

Romania and Slovakia are also blocking couriers that are slow, but they apply a manual approach: they use formulas to “highlight” possible offenders and then check courier GPS history on order level manually. This manual process takes local COPS teams from 3 to 6 hours every week. So if we could agree on metric that would be approved both by legal and HQ teams, we could reduce workload in several countries.

The main difference here is Kubecost is currently calculating based on *Unblended costs*, as it does not have access to our AWS Billing. 

If you account for this and look at the *Unblended costs* in Cost Explorer, the differences per day are usually under $500. However, whilst Kubecost is not connected to our AWS account billing, it makes some assumptions. These assumptions span a wide range of resource costs like PV’s per deployment, and thus will never truly match what we see in Cost Explorer.

If we want to dial in the difference of $500, we’d have to do some work on connecting Kubecost to our Billing in AWS.

Guidance writing rules: 

* If a document A which is cross checked against a different document B(containing source of truth documents), there is a need to define fallbacks for document B for the the cross checked fields. 
** All the source of truth documents checks will have fallbacks.
* The rules for the source of truth fields from a document should be surrounded with {{document_exists}}condition (basically will be only evaluated for renewals). See Georgia ID [example|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/d3db2a4e65a05fc5229fc3dd01bd0e5ddad07221/src/rides/driver/driver_auto_acceptance/main/auto_accept_documents/config/unified_documents_auto_acceptance/GeorgiaUnifiedRules.ts#L88-L175].
** The checks like expiry and issue dates should be run both for leads and renewals so should be defined without {{document_exists}}condition.
** If a document has no other checks other than those from {{document_exists}} add a textDefined condition checking the presence of a field.
* Use the {{fleet_ocr}}[ dynamic config |https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/dynamic-config/entity/edit/b2NyLWZsZWV0LWRvY3VtZW50cy9vY3JfZG9jdW1lbnRfY29uZmlncw==/:sharknado]to may current renewal fleet document_type to veritas document_type and side.
* It is important to correctly define source of truth fields when those fields are not populated in the registration flow, and dependent document would need to cross check with something but will fail if {{from_profile}}will be used.
** {{reg_number}} for example may be defined as {{from_profile}}as it is available in the reg flow and will be present in the context under profile section both for leads and renewals (ideally if we know the source of truth document use that one, but in order to speed up the migration it is not really critical to be migrated, for example SK rules use [it like this|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/16f15edae7b4563d89214a81409a4bdbb41928af/src/rides/driver/driver_auto_acceptance/main/auto_accept_documents/config/unified_documents_auto_acceptance/SlovakiaUnifiedRules.ts#L183-L196])

Hi [~accountid:712020:0641ea87-e832-482b-8673-ab85e9ad6441] 

In my opinion Bolt still has the right to charge the intermediation fee but that should be based on the real value of the trip, not on the 169,96 EUR value that was charged by the driver’s fault. 

The TVDE Law states that: “3 - O operador da plataforma eletrónica pode cobrar uma taxa de intermediação, a qual não pode ser superior a 25 % d+*o valor da viagem calculada nos termos dos números anteriores*+.”

This statement leads me to think that the fee can only correspond to the value corresponding to the trip itself, meaning the 12,27 EUR. I believe that charging the fee corresponding to the 169,96 EUR value could be considered an abuse of law (abuso de direito), since Bolt would be capitalizing on the driver’s mistake. 

Therefore, I believe the answer would be: we can still charge the fee, since the drive did occur and Bolt can’t be responsible for the driver's mistakes but that fee should be limited to the real trip price, otherwise Bolt could be abusing its rights.

Hey [~accountid:615d90da9cdb93007288f515] , I cannot support this new proposal as it is harsher and means more control over couriers. In particular, we cannot restrict their freedom when and how to provide services even more because [the provisional agreement on the EU Platform Workers Directive was reached on 8 February 2024 by the EU institutions|https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2024/03/11/platform-workers-council-confirms-agreement-on-new-rules-to-improve-their-working-conditions/], it means that the courier/drivers reclassification topic becomes even hotter on the EU level.   

*General rules to observe:* 

#  *Temporarily suspension of a courier*  for a few days is possible, provided (i) clear advanced information and (ii) reasons for such a suspension are communicated. Temporary suspension is regulated by clause 9.1 of T&C (if acceptance is low, we might claim damage to Bolt's brand and reputation or business due to bad user experience BUT it is not a very strong argument, I would not rely on it too heavily. Damage to Bolt’s brand and reputation is a stronger argument if we receive actual +eaters' complaints)+.
# A low acceptance rate alone is not a sufficient argument to permanently bloc a courier. *Permanent blocking* under clause 4.6 could be considered only if _“If the Courier has materially breached its obligations or has received several complaints”._ That is, if  a low acceptance is accompanied by *repetitive* complaints by eaters, courier could be permanently blocked if we provide (i) a clear advance notice, (ii) reasoning and (iii) information that the courier has the right to challenge his/her suspension under the internal complaint-handling system clause 14.2 of the [T&C for couriers.|https://assets.ctfassets.net/tk7rwcciwvbq/4TC5ah75KrZSkpkzd5nBp6/9ef85b3d18b4e16f294391dffbd20d82/V5_of_Bolt-Courier_T_C__LT__-ENG-.pdf]
## As a general rule, we can permanently block couriers only by giving notice at least 30 days in advance (clause 9.2). 
## The only exception that allows Bolt to terminate a courier without a 30-day notice is when a courier *repeatedly* breaches or fails to comply with any of the obligations set out in T&C (clause 4.4”c” of Regulation (EU) 2019/1150).

Overall, we cannot permanently block a courier only due to low AR. In light of the EU law developments, I advise you to look for *positive incentives* (some bonuses, benefits) to motivate them to increase the AR instead of punishments.

The income obtained by the franchisor from Estonia is subject to withholding tax at 10% in Estonia. The withholding tax is a legal requirement and the person who should bear this tax is the franchisor (but it is Bolt as payor who deducts it).

In your example if royalty is 10K, Bolt will withhold 1K and pay 9K net.

The 1K Estonian withholding tax should be a tax credit against the franchisors final tax liability in Poland. 

Unless the franchisor proves he cannot use the 10% tax credit, there is no need to cover the 10%.

Hi [~accountid:5f7aaad6021acf0076d55a90] after reviewing this matter and discussing with the legal product team below out thoughts on this matter:

* How legal team sees it should have been done:
** rider paid 169,96 EUR for the trip to the tvde operator
** rider has approached us with the issue
** Bolt finds out driver is at fault
** Bolt asks tvde operator to pay back the difference because the ride was indeed performed and cost 12,27 EUR
** tvde operator pays difference back to Bolt
** Bolt intermediates this money back to rider
* It seems consistent with the TVDE law in PT and our t&c that intermediation fee is still to be paid by the TVDE operator in this case since there was a transaction and a transportation service performed.
* The TVDE Law states that: “3 - The operator of the electronic platform may charge an intermediation fee, which may not exceed 25 % of the v*alue of the journey calculated in accordance with the previous paragraphs.*” This statement leads us to think that the fee can only correspond to the value corresponding to the trip itself, meaning the 12,27 EUR. Therefore charging the fee corresponding to the 169,96 EUR value could be considered an abuse of law (abuso de direito), since Bolt would be capitalizing on the driver’s mistake. 

We will pass on this risk to the commerce team that is responsible for refunds. [~accountid:5f7aaad6021acf0076d55a90] please also confirm if we have sent a response to the driver. Thank you.

Query that Avishek used for Signups

*Signups Query*

{noformat}SELECT  country_name
       ,DATE_TRUNC('month',CAST(user_created_date AS DATE))                                                         AS user_created_month
       ,COUNT(*)                                                                                                    AS total_signups
       ,SUM(CASE WHEN first_ride_date IS NOT NULL AND days_to_ftr <= 14 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)                          AS total_ftrs
       ,SUM(CASE WHEN platform = 'ios' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)                                                           AS ios_signups
       ,SUM(CASE WHEN first_ride_date IS NOT NULL AND platform = 'ios' AND days_to_ftr <= 14 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)     AS ios_ftrs
       ,SUM(CASE WHEN platform = 'android' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)                                                       AS android_signups
       ,SUM(CASE WHEN first_ride_date IS NOT NULL AND platform = 'android' AND days_to_ftr <= 14 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS android_ftrs
FROM
(
	SELECT  u.user_id
	       ,c.city_name
	       ,co.country_name
	       ,u.user_created_date
	       ,CASE WHEN u.user_app_version LIKE '%CA%'THEN 'android'
	             WHEN u.user_app_version LIKE '%CI%'THEN 'ios'
	            ELSE 'other' END AS platform
	       ,f.first_ride_date
	       ,DATE_DIFF('day',CAST(u.user_created_date AS date),CAST(f.first_ride_date AS date)) AS days_to_ftr
	FROM core_models.dim_user u
	LEFT JOIN ng_public.etl_first_ride_attribution_channel f
	ON u.user_id = f.user_id
	LEFT JOIN core_models.dim_city c
	ON c.city_id = u.user_home_city_id
	LEFT JOIN core_models.dim_country co
	ON c.country_id = co.country_id
	WHERE CAST(u.user_created_date AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE '2023-08-01' AND DATE '2024-02-29'
	AND co.country_name IN ('Paraguay', 'Netherlands', 'Nigeria', 'Kenya', 'Tanzania, United Republic of', 'Norway', 'South Africa', 'Lithuania', 'Nigeria', 'Thailand', 'Romania', 'South Africa', 'Cyprus', 'Tunisia', 'Croatia', 'Azerbaijan', 'Ukraine', 'France', 'Ghana', 'Latvia', 'United Kingdom', 'Spain', 'Finland', 'Germany', 'Slovakia', 'Portugal', 'Malta', 'United Kingdom', 'Czech Republic', 'Belgium', 'Sweden', 'Poland') 
)
GROUP BY  1
         ,2
ORDER BY 1,2{noformat}

Also:

*Low spending channels and low efficiency channels have the problem*

* steps are not intuitive, larger spends lead to same or bigger efficiency (not expected)

Solution:

* This happens, because the function get_metric_at_uc_ratio() returns *the value of the next step* (and not the actual value where ratio is achieved
* Function get_last_step_incremental_response() gives the actual incremental response for the step of the chosen length
* In cases when the curve is very steep this can result in controversial results, like:
** UC ratio at 25 Eur = 10
** UC ratio at 50 Eur = 0.1 (steep curve)
** So if you plug in the desired ratio of 4, it will give back 50 Eur as recommended spend.
** However if you use get_last_step_incremental_response at cost between 25 and 50 Eur, one can find a point where UC ratio will be 4.
** Other more visual example is

!Screenshot 2024-03-27 at 15.26.26.png|width=811,height=361!

This can potentially be fixed with:

* going for smaller step (to give the function get_metric_at_uc_ratio more options)
* working with the shape of the curve, excluding the opportunities for very steep growth in the beginning (such cases are already not very common, especially for Rider)

Please see our responses:

*2]* Data Deletion Post-Agreement Termination: Rate limits for deletion requests are imposed, restricting Bolt's rights to data deletion unless additional fees are paid. This also applies when there is termination of the DPA. Arguably can be mitigated because the data can also be anonymised without restriction, but this should be an equal choice for Bolt.



*AF Response:*

Please note that the data deletion term is a bit more nuanced:

We have invested significant efforts in the development of the tool. You are required to implement it properly and we provide comprehensive support to do that. The Rate Limits are very high, they allow customers to delete over 56.7K users per 24 hours. This means that you can delete almost 400K users per week and 1.7Mil per month.

This clause is intended to prevent a situation that a customer arrives at the last week and asks us to delete the data of millions of users which is not possible unless we dedicate several analysts to do it and that means that they are diverted from their normal tasks in improving our services. The clause is intended to balance the workload created by deletion requests. There is nothing in the GDPR or other privacy laws that prohibits us from contractually asking you to use the tool in a commercially reasonable manner. The fact we are required to delete does not mean we cannot impose certain reasonable terms for deletion. This is not a revenue stream and almost no customer which has implemented the tool properly has been charged. The number of cases that out of thousands of customers we have charged for deletion can be counted on one hand and this was only in extreme cases of customers requesting very large datasets deleted in very short timeframes. Please re-read the clause carefully and you will see it it balanced and fair and refers only to those situations detailed above which rarely happen. We are happy to assist you in the implementation of the Open DSR API.



*3]* Data Breach Notification: AppsFlyer does not commit to adhering to our mitigation instructions, and only promises to “consider” extra measures from Bolt's request. This should lead to the breach of the GDPR, as by law Applsflyer would have to 100% comply with our requests to implement additional safeguards. 



*AF Response*:

as like any SaaS vendor, we will conduct our own investigation. If a breach happens, it will not affect just one customer. We cannot receive instructions from a variety of customers. It will cause chaos. This is not possible and not market standard. We commit to remedy the situation and retrieve appropriate security.

Regarding “your expense”-we will cover our expenses in remediating the situation and ensuring appropriate security according to accepted standards. If you require additional special measures on top of the appropriate measures-this is at your expense. This is already clear from the wording.

Our policy is 72 hours. We are happy to add that.



*4]* Audit Rights Limitation: Bolt's right to request audits is restricted. AppsFlyer allows us to terminate the agreement because it reserves the right to avoid audits it deems “excessive” - which go beyond presenting Bolt with prior audit reports like SOC II or ISO27001. 

Such audits are also limited to once annually unless prompted by a data breach or regulatory inquiry. This is limiting our rights as the controller and would likely be unlawful. 

*AF Response*:

Respectfully, this is interpretation is inaccurate. We provide you a validated third party audit. There is nothing in the GDPR which prohibits the provision of a third party audit as a means to contribute to inspections. Please note that this is also the market standard.



*5]* Being notified by Applsflyer in case they receive Bolt`s unlawful instruction: “Processor must inform the controller if, in its opinion, an instruction infringes the GDPR or other Union or Member State data protection provisions” - this requirement of the GDPR is not explicitly covered by the DPA.

This is basically a formal infringement of the GDPR Art. 28 - safeguard not ensured. There is some wording to go around this obligation included in the DPA. Examples:

a) Customer specifically acknowledges and agrees that its use of the Services will not violate the rights of any Data Subject.

b) AppsFlyer shall not Process Customer Personal Data other than on the Customer’s documented reasonable and customary instructions

c) Customer instructs AppsFlyer to Process Customer Personal Data in a manner consistent with the terms of the Agreement and this DPA.



+*AF Response.*+

“We are happy to add: Processor must inform the controller if, in its opinion, an instruction infringes the GDPR or other Union or Member State data protection provisions”.

# [aedes.close|https://github.com/moscajs/aedes/blob/main/docs/Aedes.md#aedesclose-callback] should close the connections.
# We [are calling it|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-nodejs-common/blob/16bb7439e193ef6de0cf5d1ee99aff93e94e79c8/src/messaging/broker/mqtt/MqttBrokerBase.ts#L92-L96] in {{MqttBrokerBase.shutdown}}.

*Data Subject Access Request – Response* 

 

Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *14/12/2023.*

 

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others.

* *Your data on 2023-6-15 [Exported time: UTC]*

Hi [~accountid:5aab754b5c335d2a73a795f4] - just summarising what I said on our call for our records 🙂 

{color:#4c9aff}~__&*%^*&*%^&*_~{color}

From the ‘raw legal' perspective there are two aspects we are concerned with:

*(1) To the extent possible blocking should always be done ‘correctly’.* Additional guidance on this topic will be issued in the next month or so. This does not directly impact what your note/guidance says in relation to safety incidents.

In short, (a) the block needs to be for a reason that is enabled by our terms (this will be covered with safety blocks), (b) we should either issue a temporary block whilst we are investigating OR we need to be reasonably sure that a block is appropriate (c) there needs to be an email to the relevant party/parties confirming the suspension (taking into account whether the driver is a fleet driver), (d) for at least EU markets we need to link our independent drivers to our internal complaints handling portal and (e) our messaging must respect the nature of any fleet relationship i.e. Bolt does +not+ have a direct contract with fleet drivers. 

Points (a) - (c) can be summarised as: we cannot block for any reason, we are not ‘god’ and blocks must be reasonable / proportionate. I trust there is no conflict with that and your team’s existing processes, although when this new guidance is issued it will need to be integrated into your existing safety process (to the extent anything is all not already covered).

_The exception to ‘following the correct procedure’ is if circumstances are so gravely serious that there is an overwhelming need to take another action - in accordance with (2) below._

*(2) Bolt may be found to be legally liable for ‘enabling’ any harm that was foreseeable. It is worth reviewing your team's existing processes to see if they are appropriate, all things considered.*

If we know that a driver has a history of assaulting passengers and we think that this driver may continue that behaviour (or the harm is *very* serious) then we may be found to have owed that driver’s future passengers a ‘duty of care'. There will be local variances to the laws on this, but there is no need to deep dive; the principle we ought to abide by is _“if there is a terrible thing that we think is likely to happen and we have the power to stop it, we ought to stop it.”_

At the same time, we do also need to respect that the driver is generally an independent person acting on his own behalf and it may be overstepping the boundary for Bolt remove the driver from the platform for incidents which are of low significance. So it is a balancing exercise.

It is not appropriate for the legal team to prescribe our precise actions on this topic - the safety team is best place to determine the appropriate action. But I would ask the safety team to consider the following:

(i) [~accountid:5aab754b5c335d2a73a795f4] you have mentioned to me that our standard practice is to *not* contact local law enforcement for very serious criminal incidents outside of the UK and Ireland. Perhaps I had misunderstood, but if that is correct then your team should reconsider this - perhaps it *_is_* appropriate, on a case by case basis. We risk legal liability and also bad publicity at a later date if we did not take obvious steps to safeguard future passengers in this way. I make this comment in light of some of the items on your sheet being gravely serious and concerning the safety of children.

(ii) For very serious criminal incidents, we should be mindful to not prejudice any ongoing investigations. I believe this is covered for some items, but it should extend to anything else that is equally serious.

{color:#4c9aff}~__&*%^*&*%^&*_~{color}

# The agency does have investigative powers under the POCAML and powers to request for documents and information for purposes of their internal investigations. Under the Act, this power is generally exercised by the Police by virtue of court orders i.e either orders to produce documents or information or search and seizure orders. 
# In the absence of a production order-we can decline to provide the information requested until they have provided us with a court order as required under Part X of POCAML and more specifically with sections 103 and 104 of the POCAML. 
# A number of regulators/enforcement agencies do have powers to collect information for purposes of exercising their function but typically it requires that they obtain a court order to do so and most just don’t bother which is why they write these  information request as a short cut to actually getting the court order. Its no wonder that when we don’t respond, we don’t hear from them.

Before we dive in, I want to emphasise that fraud prevention tactics are very dynamic and depend on numerous data points as well as factors in order to trigger and apply. We are currently in the process of reviewing and improving (_reworking_) the triggers hence we expect more accurate targeting in the future and slight changes coming up shortly.

We use our fraud engine to check, profile and apply any decisions that we have defined. To put it briefly we have driver scheduled blocks as well as hard blocks for the driver actions. _Manually we also apply payment method removal upon need, but this is not through any systems nor automatic._ 

Then for the monetary aspects we also run checks on driver promotions/campaigns with the action to remove fraud-gained amounts. And on the order level, we have the option to revert overcharges and make a decision to close the pricing as per need (either 0 or upfront or actual price). 

You can see the most popular areas we target defined here: [https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1XKWOfdS1U1BfU5aVI93qXB8lcGGvYCeDjU9kHEZSuAw/edit#gid=0|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1XKWOfdS1U1BfU5aVI93qXB8lcGGvYCeDjU9kHEZSuAw/edit#gid=0|smart-link]

We have drivers who systematical abuse or system by overcharging our customers.

*What fraud rules do we have for overcharges?*

Main rider complaints in Sweden:

* I was charged more than expected
* I was charged unfair wait time fee
* I was wrongly charged a cancellation fee

Drivers getting multiple reports of the same nature strongly indicates fraudulent behaviour. 

* I was charged more than expected *(ending trip late)*
* I was charged unfair wait time fee *(marking arrival too early and starting trip to late)*
* I was wrongly charged a cancellation fee *(drivers not staying in the pick up spot and cancelling order after 5 min)*

We would like to implement fraud rules for these issues. Could be something like:

* If driver received X refunds → Block or no longer eligible for refunds.
* If driver has paid wait on over X% of rides → Block or no longer eligible for paid wait.
* If driver has X% of orders with cancellation fee → Block or no longer eligible for cancellation fees.
* If driver exceeds recalculation threshold on X% of rides → Block or no longer eligible for recalculations.
* If driver is receiving more than X tickets of either ATI → Block or no longer eligible for refunds.

Attaching a picture of drivers with most refunds in the past month in Sweden. It’s very easy to detect fraudulent behaviour.

Hi there!

To give a bit of context: The fraud team deals with bigger cases of financial fraud or user patterns with a significant business case. The fraud team does not look at users on an individual level unless it is a clear false positive case. And even in those cases, it is rather for us to finetune our rules and restrictions for a more positive user experience for *good* users.

Further, what you have here is a *refund/promo fraud* (social engineering) case which, in general, is overall dependent on CS processes and procedures. Think of it this way - the user is just requesting a refund/promo and we are complying, therefore, we are allowing them to financially gain. Actually, how this user ended up in your queue is due to the fraud rules flagging and rejecting automatic actions. 

Hence, I can suggest you follow your local processes in regard to users making bad reports/requesting refunds or compensations; and possibly raise this with your leads if you find issues with the processes. *It is up to you how to action the user.*

Cheers,

h1. Context

To be able to execute the configless provisioning script, we need at a minimum:

* the feature branch contents
* the {{develop}} branch contents
* all the history up to the lowest common ancestor between these two branches, to be able to compute the {{merge-base}}.

h1. First Attempt: Bring as few commits as possible (partial clone + sparse checkout)



* clone the feature branch with --depth=100 (unlikely that a feature branch is >100 commits ahead of develop)
* clone develop with --depth=1
* fetch develop incrementally with --deepen=n, to bring n extra commits each time. Experimented with various values for n

In addition, perform a sparse checkout, to only bring the relevant files from the repository:

* the {{gen/config}} directory, containing configless resource information
* the {{tooling_scripts}} needed to run configless provisioning



Here’s the process in a nutshell:

{noformat}function sparsecheckout() {
    mkdir $REPO_DIR
    cd $REPO_DIR
    git init
    git remote add origin git@github.com:bolteu/bolt-server
    git sparse-checkout set $CONFIG_DIR
    git sparse-checkout set tooling_scripts/configless
    git sparse-checkout set tooling_scripts/lib/spawn.js
    git fetch origin $MAIN_BRANCH --depth=10000
    git fetch origin $FEATURE_BRANCH --depth=100
    git checkout develop
}{noformat}



{panel:bgColor=#fffae6}
This option ended up taking even more time than the plain {{git clone}}.
{panel}

h1. Second Attempt: No Blobs + Sparse Checkout

This is the best option out of all the variations I’ve tried:

{noformat}git clone --filter=blob:none --no-checkout --no-tags <repo-url> <dir>
cd <dir>
git sparse-checkout set <only needed directories/files>
git checkout <branch>{noformat}



{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
This is the option I ended up choosing. It brought the clone time down from 7-10m to 2m.
{panel}

Hi [~accountid:60587c57109af1006886dd87] in summary to answer your question: in the case of renewals the relevant receipts issued by Identita’ through the Single Permit Portal are better records than the ‘print out’ currently being provided by Delivery Partners. Instead it is recommended that you request delivery partners/fleets (a) the confirmation that the Renewal Single Permit Application was submitted prior to the expiration of the residence card and (b) copy of the relevant receipts of submission issued by Identita’ through the Single Permit Portal. Below further detailed review. Please let me know if you have any questions.

_______________________________

*Confirming the courier can legally work in Malta*

Since Bolt is not the employer of couriers, from an immigration perspective the responsibility to ensure that the couriers are legally employed would fall on the Delivery Partner and not Bolt itself. Having said that, from a reputational perspective our current outside attorneys agree that we should still ensure that the couriers are legally employed with the Delivery Partner.

*_Scenario 1: First time applications or change of employer_*

With respect to new Single Permit Applications (whether first time applications or change of employer), +the employee is not authorized to work with the new employer during the processing of the application+ and may only commence work with the new employer once he has the formal authorisation (either in the form of the receipt confirming he may work in Malta/blue paper with the necessary stamp) or the physical single permit.

_What to check for first time applications or change of employer?_ 

* _The formal authorisation (either in the form of the receipt confirming he may work in Malta/blue paper with the necessary stamp) or_ 
* _the physical single permit._

*_Scenario 2: Renewals_*

Identita’ seems to have adopted the following approach in the context of renewal applications: +subject to the Renewal Single Permit Application being submitted prior to the expiration of the employee’s Single Permit, then that employee should be in a position to continue working during the processing of the application+, even if his Single Permit expires during the processing of the renewal application.

_What to check in the case of renewals?_

_Request the fleet (that is the employer):_

* _The confirmation that the Renewal Single Permit Application was submitted prior to the expiration of the residence card and_ 
* _A copy of the relevant receipts of submission issued by Identita’ through the Single Permit Portal_ 
** _typically the fleet - or its Organisational Manager if they outsource the handling of the applications - and the employee would immediately receive an automated email from the Agency confirming the submission of the application). Hey Nils,

Apologies for the misunderstanding.

This driver doesn’t have separate commission invoices between 11.2022 and 05.2023, because their commission sum was negative; meaning we didn’t have any commission to invoice.

This happens when a driver’s compensations/bonuses/rider discount compensations are more than their commission amount. We present such incentive amounts as a discount from their commission - which, in this driver’s case, caused negative commission because the sum of such incentives was more than his commission. Negative commission means we don’t have any commission to invoice, and in this case, we wait until the driver’s commission sum exceeds their bonuses (usually happens in few months time when they keep taking rides). Once this happens, we issue an invoice covering the whole period without an invoice. So, as you can see this driver got a commission invoice covering the period 11.2022 - 05.2023:

A note from the insurance team. This type of insurance is referred to as Goods In Transit (GIT) with a Bailee's Customer Insurance extension. However, there is normally an excess/deductible on the policy which is normally €50-€250+ depending on the nature of the businesses.

Therefore, if we are only looking at low-value items and only one item is in each vehicle then I see no need to buy insurance as it will be cheaper and quicker to reimburse any losses ourselves. 

If this changes and we want to carry higher-value items or have cars filled with parcels (Amazon style) then we can explore insurance options, or we can do what Amazon do and push the insurance requirement and cost onto the driver/vehicle owners.

{code:sql}with orders as (
select
	cpd.created						as comment_created
	, cpd.sender_type 
	, cpd.city_id
	, cpd.order_id 
	, cot.id as order_try_id
	, cot.driver_id
	, cot.state as order_state
	, cot.client_cancel_reason as client_cancellation_reason
	, cot.reject_reason as driver_cancellation_reason
	, cot.created as order_try_created
	, row_number () over (partition by cpd.created order by cot.created desc) 	as order_rw_nmbr
from comms.chat_profanity_detected as cpd
left join ng_public.company_order_try as cot
	on cpd.city_id = cot.city_id
	and cpd.order_id = cot.order_id
	and date(cot.created_date) >= date('2024-01-15')
	and cpd.created >= cot.created
where 1=1
	and cpd.sender_type = 'rider'
	and cpd.order_system = 'taxi'
	and date(cpd.created_hour) >= date('2024-01-15')
	and date(cpd.created_hour) <= date('2024-02-26')
),
orders_edited as (
select 
	o.comment_created
	, o.sender_type
	, o.city_id
	, o.order_id
	, o.order_try_id
	, o.driver_id
	, o.order_state
	, o.client_cancellation_reason
	, o.driver_cancellation_reason 
	, o.order_try_created
	, o.order_rw_nmbr
	, c.id 						as support_case_id
	, c.user_persona
	, c."source"
	, row_number () over (partition by o.order_id, o.order_try_id order by o.comment_created asc) as order_try_rw_nmbr
from orders 						 								as o
left join ng_customer_support.etl_data_api_support_case 					as c
	on o.order_id = c.order_id 
	and o.city_id = c.city_id 
	and o.driver_id = c.user_id 
	and c.user_persona = 'driver'
	and date(c.created_date) >= date('2024-01-15')
	and c."source" <> 'beehive_outgoing'
where 1=1
	and o.order_rw_nmbr = 1
)
select 
	oe.city_id
	, adcc.name as country_name
	, oe.order_id
	, oe.order_try_id
	, oe.order_state 						as order_try_state
	, oe.client_cancellation_reason
	, oe.driver_cancellation_reason
	, b.is_positive 					as driver_score_signal_is_positive
	, b.negative_rules 				as negative_rules_triggered
	, oe.driver_id
	, case when oe.support_case_id is not null then true
		else false end 				as driver_raised_case
	, oe.support_case_id				as driver_case_id
	, oe."source" 						as driver_case_source
from orders_edited as oe
left join ng_public.driver_behavior_quality_driver_behavior_quality__order 	as b
	on oe.order_id = b.order_id 
	and oe.city_id = b.city_id 
	and oe.comment_created >= b.created
	and oe.order_try_id = b.order_try_id
	and date(b.created_date) >= date('2024-01-15')
	and date(b.created_date) <= date('2024-02-26')
left join ng_public.admin_system_city as adc
	on oe.city_id = adc.id
left join ng_public.admin_system_country as adcc
	on adc.country_code = adcc.code
where 1=1
	and oe.order_try_rw_nmbr = 1{code}

Point 1 - following the same principle of t&c amendments it should be communicated 15 days in advance

POint 2 - Changes in earnings may create dissatisfaction and lead to reclassification claims. Please see below a few high level thoughts on this:

* Some months back it has been internally decided that couriers in Malta should still have visibility on earnings before accepting a delivery since it is how Bolt communicates the price to the delivery partner (even though indirectly through its employees).
* You are now considering changing base earnings for fleets - I say fleets since MT is 100% a fleet market and the earnings are not of the courier and are transfeered only to their fleets. Bolt only has a contratual relation with the fleets.
* What do those changes in base pricing consist of? Where will the app maps that share a view of what the multiplier earnings are in a certain zone will be visible? In the courier app only or also in the fleet platform?
** Generally, if these changes would not lead to determining maximum limits of earnings and would not affect autonomy of fleets then IMO the reclassification risk would be low.
** However, I would reckon essential that the comms and these maps features target fleets, allowing them to have that information. Therefore, it would seem recommended to share the multiplier earnings with fleets as well: by email and the fleet portal.

We could remove the section about how the taximeter operates, but I think there is value in describing how it works. I will attach a short description below.



The integration works as follows:

# The fleet owner adds their drivers using the Halda Integration Key (available in the driver portal for each driver) to Haldas Åkarnet.
# The driver logs in to the taxi meter using their driver code (found on the taximeter).
# When you accept a trip, the information is automatically sent to the taximeter.
# When the trip starts in the app, a fixed-price trip begins on the taximeter with the same price as in the app.
# When the trip ends, the final price is sent to the taximeter, which automatically completes the trip and prints a receipt



Swedish translation:

 Hur fungerar integrationen?

# Åkaren lägger till sina förare med Halda-integrationsnyckeln (finns i förarportalen för varje förare) i Haldas Åkarnet.
# Föraren loggar in på taxametern med sin förarkod (numret på taxiförarlegitimationen).
# När du accepterar en resa skickas informationen automatiskt till taxametern.
# När resan startas i appen går en fastprisresa igång på taxametern med samma pris som i appen.
# När resan avslutas skickas det slutgiltiga priset till taxametern och taxametern avslutar resan automatiskt samt skriver ut ett kvitto.

It’s not exactly that simple. Currently the entire element is removed from the DOM, so it cannot be animated. This doesn’t happen through any sort of component state management, though - both buttons dispatch new messages, which upon being fetched cause the component to be re-rendered and this panel to disappear. I cannot easily hide it instead of removing it from the DOM, as this component is tied to the last message and cannot exist without that message being an interaction request. The only thing which I could do is do the animation before dispatching the new message submission, but that not only doesn’t look as nice as on the video in description (attaching how it looks in reality), but also doesn’t solve the problem - the input is still being shown, just a bit later (after the animation). So it’s not a good solution.

The ultimate reason why is this input shown is that there’s some time between submitting the last interaction (i.e. the last message being the interaction reply, when we display the input) and receiving the new interaction from the service (when the last message is a subsequent interaction with the Good/Bad buttons). We could hide the input, but to do that, it would be necessary to predict that there’s another interaction upcoming, and this is currently decided solely by the service, so it’s practically not possible.

Query used on {{support-configs}} internal DB:

{code:sql}WITH newest_configs AS (
    SELECT
        name,
        MAX(version) as version
    FROM
        support_configs
    WHERE
        schema_name = 'email_routing_config' AND
        active = 1
    GROUP BY
        name
)
SELECT
    sc.id AS id,
    sc.created AS created,
    sc.name AS name,
    JSON_EXTRACT(sc.data, '$.city_id') AS city_id,
    JSON_EXTRACT(sc.data, '$.from') AS from_address,
    JSON_EXTRACT(sc.data, '$.to') AS to_address,
    JSON_EXTRACT(sc.data, '$.user_persona') AS user_persona,
    JSON_EXTRACT(sc.data, '$.tier') AS tier
FROM
    support_configs AS sc
JOIN
    newest_configs
ON
    sc.name = newest_configs.name AND
    sc.version = newest_configs.version AND
    JSON_EXTRACT(sc.data, '$.user_persona') = 'authority'
ORDER BY
    name
;{code}

Right now, the grouping seems sufficient. As any type of activity with components, we need to understand how we’re going to apply it first before going deeper and further speculating about what the grouping should be.

Here are my thoughts on potential applications of component groups:

# First of all, they give a very nice overview of the offering. When you look at the picture, it seems that we don’t own that many components, and it’s much easier to make sense of them, while looking at the list of the components itself makes you overwhelmed.
# As you can see, some of the groups have links to products not owned by us. Some groups can help us identify solutions in the same area belonging to other teams, so that we would be aware of those solutions while thinking about the future architecture or ownership.
# We can propose improvements on group level – it’s easier to notice the similarities between different components belonging to the same group. A good example is Observability – there we could use Grafana to integrate many existing solutions, even though right now they are seemingly separate.
# We could try to map some of the groups to specific tiers, to simplify the setup? For example all of the components from CI/CD group (except for Tests/Statistics) belong to tier 1-2. Same goes for Compliance and Infra support (which is mostly tier 1 actually). It doesn’t mean that we should strictly bind each group to a specific tier, but rather that we could assign a default tier to each group, but still have exceptions, which would make it somewhat easier to reason about tiers.
# Basically, for any sort of operations which are challenging to orchestrate for all of the components, we could try to execute them for component groups instead. For example, if we need to organize some sort of brainstorming across all of the components, brainstorming per component sounds ridiculous, while brainstorming per group – much more doable.
# Component groups can allow us to estimate how many dependencies we have between groups and gauge how easy it is to split the responsibility of the whole PINT into independent chunks. This can finally become a constructive argument in the discussion about… well, splitting PINT 😅 If it’s easy to demonstrate the overhead of communication between different components, which would become much more extreme if we were to split the team, it becomes a good argument against doing it.

The proposed grouping is one of the many and is likely not final. Here are some additional thoughts on the groups – either present or potential ones:

* Internal offering – it’s kinda easy to abuse this one, since a lot of things could be fit here, as the description is very vague and ambiguous. Previously it contained Directory Service, UnotiS, and R&A, which later found a better home in “Organizational management” group. Central Scheduler is kind of a weird component, so it’s better to assume that it doesn’t belong to a group than put it inside Internal offering.
* Repo setup – this one is kinda related to both backend and frontend frameworks. Local Setup is about opinionated monorepo setup for {{bolt-server}}, which is pretty much the only application for NodeJS framework. Other two components are kind of similar, but for frontend. Maybe “Repo setup” shouldn’t be a group after all. OTOH, it highlights similarities between frameworks, as both have to deal with similar things to some extent – tsconfigs, linter setup, repo setup, libraries, runtime, packaging for Builder, etc. If we’re going to keep two frameworks as separate groups (which is probably more pragmatic), it would still be a nice exercise to compare two frameworks and see if they can borrow from each other.
* Testing – a really small group now, feels like a part of NodeJS Framework, since Chaos Testing is also deeply integrated with the framework. OTOH, Chaos Testing is an actual service, while the rest of the framework is just code. But we have more services which are deeply integrated into the framework, like Dynamic Config, Secrets, Live Tracing. Maybe those could be considered a sort of “self-service” layer for services? Maybe they even deserver a separate group?



As for the groups themselves, I tried to split the components into groups, so that they wouldn’t overlap much. This is so that it would be easier to visualize the whole thing, and also so that it would be easier to make sense of our whole offering. However, you can see that some of the components are linked in several groups. While this is not great for the purposes above, it could be beneficial to try and group different components in different contexts. For example, above you saw that it could be beneficial to compare similar functionality between frontend and backend framework, so maybe it’s worth grouping it into separate groups which would slice horizontally across both frameworks? Same about “self-service”… services.

**** *Harassment:*
***** *Sexual*
***** *Race*
***** *Aggression*

 

*Stage 2 (Implementation of LLM system into Bolt’s processes).*

This stage should be discussed separately as it raises other questions, including whether Open AI is the right fit, notification to users, biases and discrimination, blocking of users, whether this is a high-risk system under new EU AI Act and we need to have additional actions to comply with the Act

{color:#ff5630}(1) {color}Generally, legal doesn’t need to get involved / approve all the various ways we look to minimise fraud on the platform. We’re happy for this activity to be carried out as a matter of course. But for what it’s worth - the initiative seems sensible 👌 🙂

_(c) there is no driver score in many markets, so those markets will need separate comms._

Let's discuss it further as I have a different perspective and want to understand yours. I will list benefits from Play Mode view please let me know what are benefits from full backlog view for new hires.

* *Access to the* *general backlog versus Play Mode view* - agents having the possibility to choose cases from all cases in the general backlog have unlimited access to cases with significant severity levels. Access of agents with Play Mode view can be limited to only low/moderate cases by assigning them to special Training Q with only those cases. This will decrease their access along with the risk of significant cases being handled by new hires.

* *Cherry picking versus Skipping* - Cherry picking of cases won't leave any trace of potential knowledge gaps or any data for trainers to follow up on. Skipping of cases will allow trainers to have visibility on which topics the agent needs retraining. Data related to skipping is not present on Safety WBRs.

* *New hires being reported after 2 months of onboarding versus new hires reported from start date -* Newly hired agents that are not added to Qs or Play Mode and Assembled won't be included in the schedule, performance trends and productive hours which will limit our visibility on their progress, their impact on entire team's performance, schedule adherence and backfilling of attrition. What is more, we won't be able to calculate if we are being billed according to what was delivered by the supplier.

*  *New hire showing higher productivity thanks to cherry*-*picking versus new hire*s *showing performance metrics according to the real knowledge consolidation -* agents that are allowed to cherry-pick will have limited knowledge on subjects they will not pick, with Play Mode view agents will need to handle a variety of subjects, also there is the possibility of picking up certain subjects that trainer believes that should be handled on the given day is possible by him as agents on Play Mode can be still be provided with case links and assign those to themselves.

The related [user|https://admin.bolt.eu/user/Users/user/187631739] of the current user was already reported to us by another agent and I already placed fraud block to the profile. 

We currently have rules in place to detect whether the eater might be a refund abuser. However, currently those decisions serve with the intention to stop the automated refunds and send them to the CS agents for manual review. That means that the decision about refunds lies with the CS.

Currently T&W and Beehive teams are working together to show fraud check decisions in Beehive and the reasons why fraud thinks that they are refund abusers to help CS assess the situation better. I believe after that we can create clear guidelines for the CS agents on how to handle these cases. Till that time, you can use the [User Calculations|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/fraud/userCalculationResults?filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A25%2C%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%22user_id%22%3A170466823%2C%22from%22%3A1708155991%2C%22check_point%22%3A%22delivery_cs_issue%22%7D%7D] page to check the decision of the fraud on the delivery refund request. When you click the [ID|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/fraud/calculations/delivery_cs_issue/11110325] on that page, then you can even see the fraud rules triggered for the eater. This eater’s refund request was rejected with the rule CS_DELIVERY_RELATED_USER_REFUNDS meaning that eater’s related eaters already had high amount of refunds and we refused the automated refund and send it to the CS ticket queue for review.  Usually, we do not advise blocking users, refusing refund should be enough. However, if you think that the eater’s sole purpose on our platform is to abuse refunds and they do not have any significant GMV even from other verticals, then you can block the eater and even place “Block for fake orders” so that the device will be blocked too. I have placed a fraud block on the user’s profile and all related profiles. That should block the accounts and block+blacklist the related devices.

I will proceed to close the ticket. Should you have any further questions or require additional assistance, please feel free to inform me by commenting on this ticket.

(ii) the Mobility Platform is 13,074,952;
and therefore well below the threshold for being designated as a “very large platform” (VLOP) under the Digital Services Act.

The numbers above are calculated based on the following principles:

* “Active recipient” is a person who has opened either the Bolt App or the Bolt Food App at least once a month within the six months preceding the publishing date.
* If a recipient is able to access the platform from a mobile application and from the webpage, we have counted this user once.
* In the context of the Mobility Platform users include riders, drivers and marketing partners.
* In the context of the Delivery Platform the users include clients, partners and couriers.

Here is the translation of the lawyer’s explanation of these articles.

{color:#0747a6}*Blue paragraph*{color}*:*

*An advocate's request* is a written appeal of an advocate to a public authority, local self-government body, their officials and employees, enterprises, institutions and organisations regardless of their form of ownership and subordination, public associations for information and copies of documents necessary for the advocate to provide legal aid to a client (part 1 of Article 24 of the Law of Ukraine "On the Bar and Practice of Law").

Legal justification of the advocate's request for the provision of documents, information and data necessary for the provision of legal aid. Representation is a type of advocacy that consists in ensuring the exercise of the client's rights and obligations in civil, commercial, administrative and constitutional proceedings, in other bodies, before individuals and legal entities, the rights and obligations of the victim, civil plaintiff, civil defendant in criminal proceedings (clause 9, part 1, Article 1 of the Law of Ukraine "On the Bar and Practice of Law");

Other types of legal aid - types of advocacy activities aimed at providing legal information, consultations and explanations on legal issues, legal support of the client's activities, drafting applications, complaints, procedural and other legal documents aimed at ensuring the exercise of the client's rights, freedoms and legitimate interests, preventing their violation, as well as facilitating their restoration in case of violation (clause 6 .part 1 of the Law of Ukraine "On the Bar and Practice of Law").

In accordance with part 1 of Article 20 of the Law of Ukraine "On the Bar and Practice of Law", in the course of practice of law, an advocate has the right to perform any actions not prohibited by law, rules of professional conduct and the legal aid agreement, which are necessary for the proper performance of the legal aid agreement, in particular:

# to make inquiries, including those concerning
obtaining copies of documents, to the state authorities, local self-government bodies, their officials and employees, enterprises, institutions, organisations, public associations, as well as to individuals (with the consent of such individuals)
# to represent and protect the rights, freedoms and interests of individuals
persons, rights and interests of legal entities in court, state authorities and local self-government bodies at enterprises, institutions, organisations regardless of their form of ownership, public associations before citizens, officials, and
officials whose powers include resolving relevant issues in Ukraine and abroad;
# to get acquainted at the enterprises, institutions and organisations with the documents and materials necessary for the Practice of Law, except for those containing information with restricted access;
# to collect information about facts that may be used as evidence, in accordance with the procedure established by law, to request, receive and withdraw things, documents, their copies, to get acquainted with them and to interview persons with their consent;
# to exercise other rights provided for by the Law of Ukraine "On the Bar and Practice of Law" and other laws.

_________________________________

{color:#bf2600}*Red paragraph*{color}:

Note:
In accordance with Article 02 of the Law of Ukraine No. 5076-VI dated 05.07.2012 "On the Bar and Practice of Law", in the course of practising law, an advocate has the right to perform any actions not prohibited by law, rules of professional conduct and legal aid agreement necessary for the proper performance of the legal aid agreement, in particular: to make advocate's requests, including for copies of documents, from state authorities, local self-government bodies, their officials and employees, and enterprises.

Pursuant to part 2 of Article 42 of the Law of Ukraine "On the Bar and Practice of Law", a public authority, local self-government body, their officials, heads of enterprises, institutions, organisations, and public associations to which an attorney's request has been sent are obliged to provide the attorney with relevant information and copies of documents no later than 5 working days from the date of receipt of the request. Refusal to provide information at the request of the advocate, untimely or incomplete provision of information, provision of information that does not correspond to reality entail liability established by law.
At the same time, I would like to clarify that under Article 212-3 of the Code of Administrative Offences, unlawful refusal to provide information, untimely or incomplete provision of information, provision of information that is untrue in response to a lawyer's request, a request from the Qualification and Disciplinary Commission of the Bar, its chamber or a member in accordance with the Law of Ukraine "On the Bar and Practice of Law" entails a fine of twenty-five to fifty tax-free minimum incomes for officials.

Hi, 

I believe this is due to a rounding issue, globally accepted accounting error. No one can do anything about it. This is a worldwide accounting concept called “rounding”. It is a glitch that is not unique to Bolt. To explain it briefly, we show the balance entries with 2 decimals in admin (i.e. 31.78), however in the system it has more decimals (i.e. 31,784). So when decimals get less, the system rounds it up/down to the closest number.

So, the system rounds the actual number up/down according to the decimals, which might result in cent differences. Our accounting system is smart enough to consider this number for the next payout.

* *Rider didn't pay for their trip* & *Rider didn't pay the full price of their trip*
** Cost?
** Countries: NG, GH, KE
** Issue: Riders can select cash payment and pay with cellular transfer (directly to the driver). If they didn’t do it, drivers reach out to us and CS writes to rider to ask them to make a payment to the drivers. Drivers don’t submit Price Reviews, CS don’t give manual compensations. 
* *My ride happened without me* & *I wasn’t dropped off at my destination*
** Cost?
** Country: UK
** Issue: CS contact the driver to inform them about the refund and that their earnings will be affected. Also to get their side of the story. 
* *I was charged twice for my order* & *I was charged more than expected* & *I didn't receive change for my payment*
** Cost?
** Countries: mostly NG, also UK, HU, TH, GH, KE
** Issue: Riders pay outside of the app (cellular transfer) or in cash and if they face any issues (paid more, paid twice, didn’t receive change) they reach out to us and CS writes to driver and asks to pay to rider. In the UK - CS reach out to driver to educate them (e.g. if driver increased the price by taking longer route on purpose).
* *My driver was impolite* & *Experience with driver didn't meet my expectations*
** Cost?
** Countries: mostly UK, also MT
** Issue: After rider’s report, CS reach out to driver to hear their side of the story, check if driver needs help and see if there was a safety case (usually if there was a conflict the driver also left a negative comment about the rider). Also CS educate the driver. 



* *Country-specific situations:*
** *Ukraine - I can't contact my driver, Driver didn't answer my calls, I want to request information about my driver:* only in Ukraine issue tags are used together with the Lost item issue tag. The outgoing ticket in the reporting is also shown on each issue tag. E.g. if 10 outgoing tickets were sent, and the incoming ticket had 3 issue tags, in the reporting it will be shown as 30 outgoing tickets (10 for each issue tag). 
** *Thailand - I want to request an affiliation letter:* CS agents calling drivers as per request from the regulators. OPS give them the list of drivers they have to call.

Apparently, we're getting these extraneous enrolments from Campaign Modals attached to the feature. They both have AND conditions: {{has_failed_sr && ff_true}} (or {{ff_false}} for old modal). However, the condition check in Campaigns has _complete_ Boolean evaluation. Meaning, {{ff_true}} is checked (and Targeting is called) even if {{has_failed_sr}} is {{false}}. Which, basically, enrols every single rider to our test.

To fix this, we would need to create a new rule, {{has_failed_sr_v2}}. A Campaigns Rule is defined in BE code, so we would be able do a proper _shorthand_ Boolean evaluation there, and thus avoid the extra enrolments.

*Data Subject Access Request – Response* 

 

Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *25/2/2024.*

 

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Hi [~accountid:62ea2a6c96eb272011a8098d] 

I was able to review the agreements.

As for *Geheimhaltungserklärung* - I think someone from legal should review it, as it's not a privacy document. I have reviewed it from the privacy side as it has some references to the privacy law, but it did not raise any concerns for me. On the other hand, I think some confidentiality provisions may be too harsh for us, but it's up for legal to decide.

As for the *Standardvertragsklauseln* - we cannot accept it because it does not properly reflect the arrangement between AVL and Bolt. It places Bolt in the position of a processor, whereas we actually remain a separate data controller. This misunderstanding is common with business clients, and we have a standard response template for this:

Response:

_“Hi [_]_

_We wanted to confirm our current data processing setup in our partnership between Bolt and AVL._

_To be clear, Bolt operates as an independent data controller when providing services to AVL. Our_[ +_General Terms and Conditions for Bolt Business_+|https://bolt.eu/en-az/legal/terms-for-business/]_, particularly section 4, state explicitly that Bolt and AVL maintain their separate data controller roles for personal data processing. Bolt fully assumes responsibility for its data processing activities, including the engagement of subprocessors, the implementation of necessary security measures for the protection of AVL's personal data, and adherence to GDPR regulations._

_To be more specific, when an AVL employee or any data subject uses Bolt Business services for a ride, they are treated as a regular user of the Bolt Rider App. The experience of these business riders is practically identical to that of standard riders, with few exceptions such as the provision of an alternative payment option (Bolt Business) and an additional ride category (Business Ride) for these users._

_The notion of controllership in our arrangement is cemented by the_ [+_EDPB Guidelines 07/2020_+|https://edpb.europa.eu/our-work-tools/our-documents/guidelines/guidelines-072020-concepts-controller-and-processor-gdpr_en] _on the concepts of controller and processor in the GDPR. Specifically, p. 25 para. 80 demonstrates this via its “_*_Example: Taxi service”._*

_Considering the above, it should be clear that Bolt independently processes all personal data of these riders as an independent controller in accordance with section 4 of our_ [+_General Terms and Conditions for Bolt Business_+|https://bolt.eu/en-az/legal/terms-for-business/] _and pursuant to our_ [+_Privacy Policy for Riders_+|https://bolt.eu/en/privacy/privacy-for-riders/#:~:text=We%20do%20not%20sell%20your,geolocation%20data%20of%20the%20passenger.]_._

_We appreciate your attention and trust that this explanation has clarified any concerns or questions you may have. If you believe our arrangement necessitates international data transfer safeguards pursuant to GDPR Art. 46 such as standard data protection clauses, we are open to cooperate on the matter.”_

ORDER by 1 ASC{noformat}

Thanks for reaching out.

In the fraud price reviews our main purpose is not to validate whether the trip is happened or not but whether the driver followed the route suggested by our app. Here driver had a trip to Narva without destination change logged in claiming that it is not possible. 

How these situations should be handled?

* If the customer refuses to make an update to their trip or there is an issue with changing the destination, the trip should be finished. The driver should not drive extra distances without the OK from us. Message should be clear -> follow the app and if app does not allow then don’t continue.
* In cases customer wants to extend or change their trip, the driver can advise that they need to update their trip info otherwise they can’t continue.

Unfortunately, there is no way to charge the payment from the user account at this point. It is up to you to decide whether to compensate the driver. Please also take a look into the KB article - [*🚗 Driver: My order price was miscalculated*|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/89334#driver-unhappy-with-a-completed-price-review] on how to advise the drivers with these issues.

Cheers,

Under the Law on Lotteries of Lithuania, a lottery is defined as a game with established rules where players buy tickets for a chance to win cash and (or) goods, and (or) gratuitous services. In accordance with the provisions of the Law on Lotteries, a game is considered to be a lottery if it meets +all+ the following criteria: 1) players buy tickets; 2) players participate in a game based on chance / success; 3) players risk to lose the amount paid for a ticket.

Here, it does not seem to me that players will lose money, also there is no need to purchase any ticket. Irrespective of how you call it, the conditions of the game do not qualify it as a lottery under the Law of Lithuania that would require approval.

To reproduce:

# Open the app, get the token by logging in with social account
# Leave the app for 1h (this is default Google token expiry time)
# Log out
# Sign up with phone number for any testing (+32770000XXXX), not exiting account.
# Choose “continue with social account”
# Profile is created with proper data, but the social account is not bound. You can recognise it by checking that email is not verified.

The DSA Regulation does not require this document, nor does the TVDE regime. In order for Bolt to fulfil its obligations under the TVDE regime, our understanding is that it is not necessary to request such documents. In particular, according to Article 9 (2) of the TVDE regime, the TVDE operator must comply with all legal and regulatory obligations relevant to the exercise of its activity, including those arising the social security legislation, but there is no legal mechanism established in this regime assigning Bolt the duty to verify compliance with such an obligation. 

Therefore this document is not legally mandatory and the business advantage of requesting it is to assess the financial risk when contracting with the traders, that is, the fleets/tvde operators.
